registry.label: Query Builder
registry.desc: Select, filter, sort, join, and compute columns — full SQL-like interface.
registry.defaults_r:
list(primary_table = NULL, joins = list(), libraries = character(0), 
    computed = list(), filters = list(), having = list(), select = list(), 
    sorts = list(), distinct = FALSE, output_name = "result")
registry.help: The full query interface: pick output columns with aliases and aggregate functions (selecting any aggregate switches to GROUP BY mode), build AND/OR filter conditions with type-aware operators (BETWEEN, IN, LIKE, NULL checks), add HAVING conditions on aggregated columns, sort by multiple keys, join additional tables (left, inner, right, full, cross), define computed columns with R expressions, and toggle DISTINCT. Generates a readable dplyr pipeline.

registry.label: Script
registry.desc: Run arbitrary R code as a pipeline step. All flow tables are available as variables.

defaults.code:
# Write your R code here.
# Declared inputs are available as variables.
# Assign values to declared output variables to save them.

registry.defaults_r:
list(input_tables = character(0), code = "# Write your R code here.
# Declared inputs are available as variables.
# Assign values to declared output variables to save them.
", 
    output_name = "result", output_defs = list(list(name = "result", 
        kind = "auto")), language = "R")
registry.help: Runs arbitrary R code as a pipeline step. Declare input tables to control run order; they become variables in the script environment. Declare any number of outputs as 'name: kind' lines (table, model, plot, image, object, or auto-detected) — each is saved to the flow and available downstream. Console output is captured and shown.

registry.label: Branch
registry.desc: Evaluate conditions and route execution to one or more downstream paths.
registry.defaults_r:
list(dependencies = character(0), paths = list(list(id = "true", 
    label = "True", token = "result_true", condition = list(op = "and", 
        rules = list(list(kind = "custom", expr = "TRUE")), groups = list())), 
    list(id = "else", label = "Else", token = "result_else", 
        else_path = TRUE, condition = list(op = "and", rules = list(), 
            groups = list()))))
registry.help: Routes execution through named path tokens. In Setup, choose the inputs the branch reads, set the number of outgoing paths, and configure each path with a label, token, and condition type such as row count, column value, task status, parameter value, or custom R expression. Downstream task panels show a 'Run after branch/loop path' selector; choose the matching path token there. Run Flow evaluates the branch and marks non-matching downstream paths as skipped.

registry.label: Loop
registry.desc: Define repeated execution over files, datasets, groups, parameters, dates, or queries.
registry.defaults_r:
list(iteration_type = "parameter_list", source = "", values = "item1\nitem2", 
    variable = "item", output_token = "result_each", naming_rule = "{task}_{item}", 
    group_col = "")
registry.help: Defines repeated execution over files, datasets, groups, parameter lists, date ranges, or database query results. In Setup, choose the iteration type, fill in the source-specific fields, name the loop variable, and keep the path token for downstream tasks inside the loop. Use the downstream task's 'Run after branch/loop path' selector to attach that task to the loop token. Preview loop validates the source and lists the iterations before the flow is run.

registry.label: Append Table
registry.desc: Stack two or more tables row-wise (dplyr::bind_rows).
registry.defaults_r:
list(input_tables = character(0), table_names = list(), id_col = "",

registry.help: Stacks two or more tables row-wise with dplyr::bind_rows(). Optionally adds a source-ID column (with editable labels per table) so you can trace which table each row came from; mismatched columns are filled with NA.

registry.label: Compare Data
registry.desc: Compare two tables using waldo and return readable differences.
registry.defaults_r:
list(table_a = NULL, table_b = NULL, by_cols = character(0), 
    output_name = "result")
registry.help: Compares two tables with waldo::compare(), optionally sorting both by key columns first so row order differences don't mask real changes. The result is a comparison object with a colour-coded added/removed preview — useful for validating a refactored step or a data refresh.

registry.label: Filter and Sort
registry.desc: Lightweight filter + sort without joins or computed columns.
registry.defaults_r: list(input_table = NULL, filters = list(), sorts = list(), output_name = "result")
registry.help: Row filtering and ordering without the full Query Builder: build AND/OR conditions with operators that adapt to each column's type, then sort by any number of columns ascending or descending.

registry.help: Wide to long: choose the columns to stack and the names for the new key/value pair (tidyr::pivot_longer). The classic first step before grouped summaries or faceted plots.

registry.help: Long to wide: values of one column become new column headers, filled from a value column (tidyr::pivot_wider); optional ID columns define the rows.

registry.label: Transpose
registry.desc: Transpose rows and columns (t()).
registry.defaults_r: list(input_table = NULL, id_col = NULL, output_name = "result")
registry.help: Swaps rows and columns with t(). An optional ID column supplies the new column headers. Because a matrix has one type, mixed-type tables are coerced to character.

registry.help: Maps old values to new ones via a rule table, with an optional NA rule ('NA' as the match value) and an else value for unmatched entries. The recoded column is always character, which avoids silent type coercion surprises.
